analysis:
This PR changes documentation only. In docs/provider/cli-reference.md it bumps the date at line 3 and adds one passthrough-table row at head line 1741 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED. In docs/reference/configuration.md it bumps the date and adds a matching env-var row at head line 414. No code, auth, attestation, encryption, coordinator wire or key-handling behavior changes.

The documented variable selects a Gated DeltaNet prompt kernel for Qwen3.5-family models, with values 0/false/no/off for stock, packed or rows to force a kernel, and probe otherwise. I found no new security surface in the documentation. It is an inference-kernel performance and numerical-equivalence control, not a trust or authorization control. The docs say the default probe keeps the four-row kernel only where it reproduces the stock result bit for bit, which is a correctness property and not a confidentiality one.

Two caveats for the next pass. First, the cli-reference row sits in the table headed by the statement that darkbloom start copies only these listed variables into the LaunchAgent plist. The row says only 'Read by' and does not state whether it is forwarded; the table is titled 'Variable | Read by'. That placement could imply daemon passthrough. This is a doc-accuracy matter, and I can't verify the actual LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvKeys list. The operator-controlled environment sits within the provider operator's own trust (ADV-001 can already modify local behavior; T-013/T-034 rely on attestation and code identity, not env). A forced kernel could in principle affect output numerics, which falls under T-007 and T-056, but those already state that correct computation is not attested.

Second, the configuration.md patch excerpt is truncated, so the full text of the added row was not visible to me. The corresponding source (GatedDelta.swift) was not supplied, so the claimed bit-for-bit equivalence and the mode parsing are unverified.

No threat-model update is needed from the supplied evidence.
